question_original: What could help conservation of the oceans?
question_scientific_reframing: How can an equity-constrained, climate-robust, land-sea intervention portfolio reduce nutrient and plastic pressure while protecting coastal ecosystem function and livelihood safeguards in a specified coastal seascape?

selected_idea.title: CoastWeave: An Equity-Constrained, Climate-Robust Portfolio Model for Land-Sea Coastal Conservation
selected_idea.central_claim: Ecological scores cannot compensate for missing observability, implementation capacity, procedural legitimacy, or livelihood/equity safeguards.

final_conclusion: Ocean conservation is better approached as a conditional, place-sensitive portfolio-design problem than as a search for one universal intervention. CoastWeave organizes nutrient reduction, plastic prevention, habitat stewardship, area-based fisheries management, observing, and capacity-building while requiring climate, capacity, legitimacy, and equity gates. It identifies decision readiness or abstention; it does not demonstrate that an actual coast has improved.

known_risks: Literature relevance, gap interpretation, and framework scoring require expert appraisal.
Artifact traceability and provenance do not establish scientific truth or local applicability.
The proposal intentionally provides no real-world intervention outcome or empirical feedback loop.
